subject: Re: Dedicated commit true-up & shortfall proposal
messages:
From: Jill Sullivan <j.sullivan@atlashealth.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@atlashealth.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated commit true-up — shortfall question

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick follow-up from our procurement side: the internal finance team is nervous about the commit true-up mechanics you outlined. Specifically they want clarity on how shortfall months are handled if Atlas underutilizes the reserved pool in Q3 during an implementation ramp. Are we charged the full committed spend immediately, or is there a soft recovery period (bridge months) where we can true-up against future usage?

Can you confirm whether there is an option for a 2-month bridge period and whether conversion credits from our hosted usage can offset shortfalls during that window? Also please include any precedent you have for partial rollbacks or credit schedules — our CFO asked for a short example in writing.

Thanks,
Jill
Jill Sullivan
Head of Procurement — Atlas Health
j.sullivan@atlashealth.com

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jill Sullivan <j.sullivan@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit true-up — shortfall question

Jill —

Appreciate the clear question. Short answer: we support a limited bridge period and allow hosted-to-dedicated conversion credits to offset shortfalls, but the exact structure depends on the committed capacity tier and the length of the contract.

Key points for Atlas (high-level):
- Bridge months: standard offering is a 1-month bridge on full commitments; for Enterprise deals we can extend to 2 months with a modest fee/discount adjustment. That gives you runway while ramping.
- Conversion credits: hosted consumption credits can be applied against committed spend during the bridge months up to the hosted-to-dedicated conversion credit pool agreed in the SOW.
- True-up mechanics: after the bridge period, any remaining shortfall is invoiced pro-rata across the immediately following quarter unless we agree an alternative true-up schedule in the contract.

I'm looping Ben (sales lead) and Marcus (pricing) to propose a concrete schedule and an example calculation. We'll follow up with a one-page proposal and the calculation sheet.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jill Sullivan <j.sullivan@atlashealth.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 12:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit true-up — shortfall question

Jill —

Thanks for flagging this. Attached is a short worked example (see commit-trueup-calculation-sheet.xlsx) and a narrative (redwood_dedicated_shortfall_proposal_v2.pdf). Summary in plain language:

Example scenario (Atlas, 12-month commit):
- Committed monthly baseline: $120k (reserved GPU pool sizing for target throughput)
- Ramp months (month 1–2) actual hosted usage converted to dedicated credits: $40k applied in month 1, $30k in month 2
- Bridge period: we offer 2 months for this deal (per Kimberly's note) where conversion credits are fully applied; during these 2 months we invoice at committed rate but apply credits, resulting in net invoice reduced by credit amount
- Post-bridge shortfall: if committed minus applied credits > 0 after bridge, remaining shortfall is split evenly across the following 3 invoice cycles (quarters) to soften impact

Net impact for Atlas in this scenario: immediate cashflow protection via credits in bridge months, and smoothing of any remainder across subsequent invoices. We can tweak the smoothing window (2–4 cycles) in the contract.

Open items for the SOW: exact maximum conversion credit pool (we proposed $150k in our term sheet), whether the bridge is fee-free or has a 5% surcharge, and the smoothing window length.

If you like, we can convert this into a simple clause for Procurement and legal to insert into the MSA.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachments: commit-trueup-calculation-sheet.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), redwood_dedicated_shortfall_proposal_v2.pdf (PDF stub)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jill Sullivan <j.sullivan@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@atlashealth.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit true-up — shortfall question

Jill / Procurement team —

Following up with a consolidated proposal so your CFO/legal can review quickly. Attached are the two stubs Ben mentioned plus a one-paragraph contract clause you can drop into the SOW. Highlights:

1) Bridge period: 2 months (fee-free) for this deal only — allows Atlas to ramp without immediate shortfall billing.
2) Conversion credits: up to $150k of hosted-to-dedicated conversion credits will be applied first during bridge months. Any unused credits after bridge are forfeited unless otherwise agreed.
3) Post-bridge true-up: remaining shortfall (committed spend less actuals and applied credits) will be amortized evenly over the next three monthly invoices.
4) SLA/throughput guarantee: we will guarantee 99th percentile tail latency for the reserved pool at the committed throughput; failure to meet guarantees triggers service credits (standard SLA language attached).

Action items:
- Procurement: confirm that the 2-month fee-free bridge + $150k credit pool is acceptable, or propose alternate smoothing window.
- Redwood: we'll draft the clause and redline to your MSA once procurement confirms high-level approval.

If helpful, I can set a 30-minute call tomorrow with Marcus to walk the CFO through the calculation.

Best regards,
Kimberly

Attachments referenced: redwood_dedicated_shortfall_proposal_v2.pdf, commit-trueup-calculation-sheet.xlsx
